note: Topical PDE4 inhibitors reached psoriasis on a mouse phorbol-ester ear-edema model and PBMC cytokine assays; crisaborole's bilateral plaque trials matched, its Phase-3-design trial did not, and no member went further in psoriasis (apremilast and roflumilast are outside this member list).
label: Psoriasis (PDE4, topical)

engagement.model: Human PBMC cytokine release (LPS/PHA/ConA-stimulated) and PDE4 enzyme assay
engagement.note: Crisaborole was selected on PDE4 inhibition and cytokine-release suppression in stimulated PBMCs; no psoriasis patient PD readout has been compared with it.
engagement.short: PBMC cytokine readout never checked in psoriasis
engagement.quote: A series of phenoxy benzoxaboroles were synthesized and screened for their inhibitory activity against PDE4 and cytokine release.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The FDA pharmacology review (model filed) names the LPS/PHA/concanavalin A-stimulated PBMC cytokine assays.
engagement.judgement: The psoriasis plaque test NCT00762658 (2007) measured sonographic infiltrate thickness but posted no results, and Nazarian 2009 (a review, not a source) reports only 'significant effects on markers of efficacy'. Crisaborole lesional biomarker work exists in atopic dermatitis (Bissonnette 2019, doi 10.1016/j.jaci.2019.06.047) and LEO 29102 has human skin-explant cAMP engagement data for atopic dermatitis (doi 10.1007/s11095-020-02962-1); neither is psoriasis and engagement does not import across diseases, so the cell stays untested.

engagement.model: Human Th17-driven ex vivo skin inflammation model (InflammaSkin; LEO 29102 cream 2.5 mg/g)
engagement.note: The model's PD readout, IL-17A/IL-22/IFN-gamma secretion from human skin explants, was never measured in LEO 29102-treated psoriasis patients; the plaque test scored clinical signs only.
engagement.short: Explant cytokine readout never measured in patients
engagement.quote: Two treatments were used in this study: a gel containing 0.5 mg/g betamethasone dipropionate (BDP) and a cream containing 2.5 mg/g LEO 29102, a PDE4 inhibitor which showed efficacy in a four week psoriasis plaque study (NCT00875277).
engagement.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC7693225). The only LEO 29102 skin PD work in people (open-flow microperfusion cAMP, doi 10.1007/s11095-020-02962-1) is atopic dermatitis and does not import.
engagement.reason: No skin-cytokine PD in LEO 29102 patients
engagement.judgement: Opens the track at its first public use (Jardet 2020, online 2020-08-25; the model was built at Genoskin/LEO before that, publication is the proxy). The readout is secreted cytokines downstream of PDE4/cAMP. NCT00875277 (2009) and NCT01466478 (2011) recorded no lesional cytokine or cAMP measure, so there is nothing to compare.

dose.note: Mouse ear edema gives a per-cent inhibition at a formulation strength, not an exposure target; 5% ointment inhibited edema 74%.
dose.short: Mouse ear edema sets strength, not exposure
dose.quote: exhibited significant anti-inflammatory activity in mouse phorbol ester ear edema model; inhibition by the proposed clinical formulation (AN2728 ointment) was 74 percent.
dose.confidence_note: Formulation names are redacted (b)(4) in the review; the strength tested was 5%.
dose.judgement: Year is the Akama 2009 publication, the earliest public account of the model; the FDA review is 2016 and covers the psoriasis IND (077537, December 2010) as well as atopic dermatitis. A topical has no systemic exposure target: the regimen carried into patients was the ointment strength (5%, then 2%) applied twice daily.

dose.note: The 2% and 5% strengths the mouse model ranked were applied to plaques; 2% twice daily beat vehicle on OTPSS at 6 weeks (54.1% vs 2.7%).
dose.quote: Percentage of Participants With Greater Decrease In Overall Target Plaque Severity Score (OTPSS): Ointment (2% Twice Daily), Vehicle: ointment treated plaque vs. vehicle treated plaque 54.1; vehicle treated plaque vs. ointment treated plaque 2.7; P<0.001.
dose.confidence_note: Registry tabular record quoted as fields. The result was first public in Anacor's 15 June 2010 press release (news-medical reprint), which gives P<0.001 for the 2.0% twice-daily primary but no percentages.
dose.judgement: Dose follows efficacy: the regimen the model ranked (ointment strength, twice daily) was reached and the bilateral trial responded. Year is the June 2010 press release; the registry (tier 3, posted 2017-03-07) sets the status. Bilateral intra-patient design, 145 subjects.
dose.magnitude_basis: plaque responder rate vs per-cent ear-edema inhibition

dose.note: Same 2% twice-daily regimen under Phase-3 conditions: PGA success 17.4% vs 13.6% at day 84; the psoriasis Phase 3 was never run.
dose.quote: Percentage of Participants Who Achieved Success in Physician's Global Assessment (PGA) of Disease Severity at Day 84: AN2728 Ointment, 2% 17.4 (6.4 to 28.3); AN2728 Ointment, Vehicle 13.6 (0.0 to 28.0); difference 3.8 (-14.3 to 21.8).
dose.confidence_note: Registry tabular record quoted as fields; 68 subjects, not powered.
dose.judgement: Scored by the v3 table 'reached, failed, abandoned': the 8-K of 27 June 2011 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1411158/000110465911037156/a11-16064_1ex99d1.htm) called the trial positive ('At the end of treatment (Day 84), 17% of the subjects in the AN2728 arm met PGA Success, while 14% of the vehicle group met that standard') and said it was not powered, but the registry CI spans zero and Anacor never ran the psoriasis Phase 3 it had an SPA for (10-K filed 2012-03-15), moving crisaborole to atopic dermatitis. Year is the 8-K; the registry (posted 2017-03-07) sets the status.

efficacy.note: AN2728 was picked on PDE4 potency, cytokine release and mouse ear-edema inhibition: an irritant model, not a psoriasis model.
efficacy.quote: 5-(4-Cyanophenoxy)-2,3-dihydro-1-hydroxy-2,1-benzoxaborole (AN2728) showed potent activity both in vitro and in vivo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the in vivo model is named in the FDA pharmacology review (mouse phorbol ester ear edema, 74% inhibition by the clinical ointment).
efficacy.judgement: Psoriasis trials began in November 2007 (NCT00762658, NCT00759161), before the model was published; model_first_use_year is the 2009 publication as a proxy.

efficacy.note: Bilateral plaque trials responded: 5% ointment 68.6% vs 5.7% (2008) and 2% twice daily 54.1% vs 2.7% greater OTPSS decrease (P<0.001).
efficacy.short: Plaques cleared more than vehicle plaques
efficacy.quote: Percentage of Participants With Greater Decrease In Overall Target Plaque Severity Score (OTPSS): Ointment (2% Twice Daily), Vehicle: ointment treated plaque vs. vehicle treated plaque 54.1; vehicle treated plaque vs. ointment treated plaque 2.7; P<0.001.
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry tabular record quoted as fields; first public in Anacor's 15 June 2010 press release (https://www.news-medical.net/news/20100615/Positive-clinical-trial-results-for-Anacor-Pharmaceuticals-AN2728-announced.aspx: 'in the 2.0% AN2728 twice daily dosing group (P <0.001), which was the primary endpoint of the trial').
efficacy.judgement: Paired comparison: the mouse model predicts anti-inflammatory activity, not a psoriasis effect size, so magnitude is direction only. A third bilateral trial (NCT00755196, 5%, 12 weeks, n=30) missed (53.3% vs 30.0%, P=0.23) and does not change the call. Year is the June 2010 press release; the registry record (posted 2017-03-07) sets the status. Apremilast and roflumilast are not members of this tile and are not scored.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: plaque responder rate vs per-cent ear-edema inhibition

patient_trials.quote: Percentage of Participants With Greater Decrease in Overall Target Plaque Severity Score (OTPSS) at Day 28: ointment treated plaque vs. vehicle treated plaque 68.6; vehicle treated plaque vs. ointment treated plaque 5.7; P<0.001.

Percentage of Participants With Lowering of Overall Target Plaque Severity Score (OTPSS) at Day 84: ointment treated plaque vs. vehicle treated plaque 53.3; vehicle treated plaque vs. ointment treated plaque 30.0; P=0.23.
Percentage of Participants With Greater Decrease In Overall Target Plaque Severity Score (OTPSS): Ointment (2% Twice Daily), Vehicle: 54.1 vs 2.7; P<0.001.

efficacy.note: Phase-3-design trial: PGA success 17.4% vs 13.6% at day 84 (CI -14.3 to 21.8); Anacor shelved psoriasis for atopic dermatitis.
efficacy.quote: Percentage of Participants Who Achieved Success in Physician's Global Assessment (PGA) of Disease Severity at Day 84: AN2728 Ointment, 2% 17.4 (6.4 to 28.3); AN2728 Ointment, Vehicle 13.6 (0.0 to 28.0); difference 3.8 (-14.3 to 21.8).
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry tabular record quoted as fields; 68 subjects, 2:1, not powered, so the miss is itself uncertain.
efficacy.reason: Mouse edema did not predict plaque clearance
efficacy.judgement: Called contra on the registry primary, not on the sponsor's 'positive preliminary results' 8-K of 27 June 2011 (decision 13); one drug's contra beats the earlier same on the track. Anacor filed an SPA for psoriasis Phase 3 (10-K 2012) but never ran it and took crisaborole to atopic dermatitis, where it was approved in 2016; Pfizer never pursued psoriasis. The sibling AN2898 was never taken into psoriasis. Year is the 8-K; the registry record (posted 2017-03-07) sets the status.

patient_trials.quote: Percentage of Participants Who Achieved Success in Physician's Global Assessment (PGA) of Disease Severity at Day 84: 17.4 vs 13.6; difference 3.8 (-14.3 to 21.8).

efficacy.model: In-vitro PDE4 enzyme and cellular assays with skin-delivery design (LEO soft-drug program)
efficacy.note: LEO 29102 was optimised on PDE4 potency, selectivity and skin delivery; the paper reports clinical efficacy in atopic dermatitis, not psoriasis.
efficacy.short: LEO soft-drug assays; AD efficacy only
efficacy.quote: This effort culminated in identification of LEO 29102 (20), a potent, selective, and soft-drug PDE4 inhibitor with properties suitable for patient-friendly formulations giving efficient drug delivery to the skin.
efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled abstract only; which cellular or in vivo models were used is not stated in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Separate track: a different sponsor's system (in-vitro PDE4/cellular assays and skin delivery, no animal model named) making a different prediction (a soft drug that acts in skin without systemic PDE4 effects). LEO 29102 entered a psoriasis plaque test in April 2009, before this 2014 publication; model_first_use_year is the publication as a proxy. The 2020 human skin-explant microperfusion work (doi 10.1007/s11095-020-02962-1) is an atopic dermatitis retrodiction and is not scored here.

efficacy.model: In-vitro PDE4 enzyme and cellular assays with skin-delivery design (LEO soft-drug program)
efficacy.note: Plaque test: LEO 29102 cream cut total clinical score 3.04 vs 1.60 for vehicle (P<0.001) but less than betamethasone (4.96); no further psoriasis trial.
efficacy.short: Plaque test beat vehicle, trailed steroid
efficacy.quote: Change in Total Clinical Score (TCS) of the Clinical Symptoms Compared to Baseline (Day 1): LEO 29102 Cream Vehicle -1.60; LEO 29102 Cream -3.04; Betamethasone Dipropionate Cream -4.96; Daivobet Ointment -6.10; vehicle vs LEO 29102 cream P<0.001.
efficacy.confidence_note: Model side abstract-level; patient side is a 24-subject, 4-week micro-plaque assay (registry tabular record quoted as fields), not a whole-body trial.
efficacy.judgement: The 2009 plaque test is the only psoriasis trial of LEO 29102 (NCT01466478, 2011, was a formulation study without posted results); its registered primary responded, so the track is same in direction, but the effect was well short of the steroid comparators (betamethasone -4.96, P<0.001 vs LEO 29102) and LEO took the compound to atopic dermatitis instead. Year is the registry posting (2019-12-11), the first public release of the result; the paired model side is Felding 2014.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: total clinical score change vs vehicle

patient_trials.quote: Change in Total Clinical Score (TCS) of the Clinical Symptoms Compared to Baseline (Day 1): LEO 29102 Cream Vehicle -1.60; LEO 29102 Cream -3.04; P<0.001.

efficacy.model: Imiquimod psoriasis-like mouse (topical DRM02), with phorbol-ester ear and Th2 contact-hypersensitivity models
efficacy.note: DRM02 cleared imiquimod psoriasiform skin and Th17 cytokines in mice, published six years after its gel failed to beat vehicle in proof-of-concept patients.
efficacy.short: Imiquimod mouse worked; patients did not
efficacy.quote: Initial efficacy data in proof-of-concept clinical trials indicated that DRM02 gel was not more effective than vehicle-only gel, and as a result, the program returned to preclinical development.
efficacy.confidence_note: The 10-K pools the psoriasis, atopic dermatitis and rosacea proof-of-concept trials and gives no numbers; NCT01993433 (psoriasis, n=23, 2013-14, primary: change in Physician's Lesion Assessment at week 6) has no posted results. Model side abstract-level.
efficacy.reason: Mouse psoriasiform model missed patient failure
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: the mouse paper (doi 10.1080/21688370.2020.1765633; 'DRM02 also decreased cutaneous clinical changes and expression of Th17 immune pathway cytokines in a mouse model of psoriasis evoked by repeated topical imiquimod application') appeared in 2020, after the 2014 trials; whether the mouse work predates the trials cannot be told from the abstract. It did not reproduce the human result, so contra by decision 10. Separate track from the phorbol-ester model because it is a psoriasis-specific (IL-23/Th17) system making a disease-specific prediction; the same paper's phorbol-ester result would score the same way. Patient side is tier 5 only, hence trial_unreported. epub_year and print_year are the model paper, which dates the comparison.

efficacy.model: Human Th17-driven ex vivo skin inflammation model (InflammaSkin; LEO 29102 cream 2.5 mg/g)
efficacy.note: LEO 29102 cream cut IL-17A/IL-22/IFN-gamma in Th17-activated human skin explants, published with the 2009 plaque-test result already known and cited as its clinical anchor.
efficacy.short: Human Th17 explant reproduced plaque-test win
efficacy.quote: Compared with the untreated InflammaSkin® model and placebo controls, the levels of IL-17A, IL-22 and IFN-γ were significantly inhibited by treatment with the PDE4 inhibitor applied in the prophylactic setting (Figure 4A).
efficacy.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC7693225); hyphens in the cytokine names are non-breaking in the source. Prophylactic setting (drug from day 0) was significant versus placebo cream; in the therapeutic setting (day 4-6) the placebo cream itself lowered IL-17A/IL-22/IFN-gamma 'comparable to the effect by the PDE4 inhibitor cream' (Figure S4), so the vehicle-controlled therapeutic effect the plaque test showed is not reproduced. Patient side is the 24-subject micro-plaque test (registry record, posted 2019-12-11), the only psoriasis trial of LEO 29102.
efficacy.reason: Explant matched plaque test, prophylactic arm only
efficacy.judgement: Separate track by the identity rule: a different model (intact human skin with skin-resident T cells activated in situ by anti-CD3/CD28 under IL-1beta/IL-23/TGF-beta, Th17 signature and keratinocyte S100A7/K16) making a different prediction (suppression of the IL-23/IL-17 axis in human tissue) from the LEO in-vitro PDE4 potency and skin-delivery assays already tracked. Retrodiction: online 2020-08-25, eleven years after NCT00875277 (start 2009-04, results posted 2019-12-11), and the paper itself names that plaque study as LEO 29102's clinical credential, so comparison_stated is true and the status is retro, never same (decision 10). source_calls_it partial because the vehicle-controlled effect held only in the prophylactic regimen; magnitude is direction only (cytokine inhibition versus a 3.04 vs 1.60 total-clinical-score change). Rule question for the checker: whether a retrodiction whose therapeutic arm is vehicle-confounded is retro with partial, as scored, or unresolved. No crisaborole or DRM02 was run in this system.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: ex vivo skin IL-17A/IL-22/IFN-gamma inhibition vs plaque-test total clinical score change

patient_trials.quote: Change in Total Clinical Score (TCS) of the Clinical Symptoms Compared to Baseline (Day 1): LEO 29102 Cream Vehicle -1.60; LEO 29102 Cream -3.04; P<0.001.

safety.model: Rabbit primary skin irritation and mouse local lymph node assay (2% ointment)
safety.note: Rabbit skin assays rated 2% crisaborole ointment a mild-to-moderate irritant; mouse LLNA showed no sensitisation. In the IND from 2008.
safety.quote: In primary ocular and skin irritation assays in rabbits, 2% AN2728 ointment was tested as a mild to moderate irritant.
safety.judgement: Year is the first IND (102317, received 2008) the review cites as covering the short-term animal studies; the review itself is 2016. The rat 6-month oral and minipig 9-month dermal studies found no systemic toxicity and are the margin side, not a harm prediction.

safety.model: Rabbit primary skin irritation and mouse local lymph node assay (2% ointment)
safety.note: Psoriasis Phase 2b: contact dermatitis 4/46, erythema 2/46, pruritus 2/46 on crisaborole vs 0/22 on vehicle; no systemic harm, as the animals said.
safety.quote: Dermatitis contact: AN2728 Ointment, 2% 4 of 46; AN2728 Ointment, Vehicle 0 of 22. Erythema: 2 of 46 vs 0 of 22. Pruritus: 2 of 46 vs 0 of 22.
safety.confidence_note: Small trial; adverse-event table counts (registry record quoted as fields), no statistics.
safety.judgement: Paired by me from the registry adverse-event table; the 8-K of 27 June 2011 reported 'contact dermatitis (8.7% in the AN2728 group)', the earliest public date. The 145-subject dose-ranging trial NCT01029405 showed the same pattern at 2% twice daily (contact dermatitis 3/37, pruritus 6/37, no serious events). No systemic adverse event was attributed to crisaborole in the psoriasis trials, consistent with the rat and minipig NOAELs. The 2016 atopic dermatitis label's application-site pain (4% vs 1%) is the same harm in another disease and is not needed to score.
